summary: Well-scoped module. MetadataRequest v1 unauth (T1). ApiVersions release-line fingerprint (T0). KIP-43 SaslHandshake probe with bogus mechanism to solicit enabled_mechanisms (T1 — a real, deterministic enumeration probe). Missing: no SCRAM/PLAIN spray, no consumer-fetch on leaked topics.

findings.title_pattern: Kafka broker returns metadata without authentication
findings.tier_evidence: MetadataRequest v1 succeeds only against a broker with no SASL/mTLS gate — deterministic vuln signal. Real broker+topic list returned.
findings.promotion_notes: Send a real Fetch v0 against one leaked topic and pull first N records — proves data-plane read without auth.
findings.tester_next_step: kcat -L -b IP:9092  ; then: kcat -C -b IP:9092 -t <leaked-topic> -o beginning -c 20  # read messages

findings.promotion_notes: Posture; SASL enumeration handles the rest.
findings.tester_next_step: kcat -L -b IP:9092 -X security.protocol=SASL_SSL -X sasl.mechanisms=PLAIN -X sasl.username=<user> -X sasl.password=<pw>
kcat -L -b IP:9092 ; correlate release with KEV/CVE database

findings.tier_evidence: KIP-43 says the server unconditionally returns enabled_mechanisms on UNSUPPORTED_SASL_MECHANISM — recce sends a nonsense mechanism and captures the real list. Deterministic, non-destructive.
findings.promotion_notes: For PLAIN: send SaslAuthenticate with candidate <user>:<pw> pairs from cred_store / known_users. If SCRAM: implement the SCRAM-SHA-256 exchange for cred spray (proper handshake, not destructive).
findings.tester_next_step: kcat -L -b IP:9092 -X security.protocol=SASL_PLAINTEXT -X sasl.mechanism=<from-list> -X sasl.username=<user> -X sasl.password=<pw>
